items.title: P&G Gillette finalized the 232 A Street purchase for its new Boston headquarters and innovation center
items.description: Breakthrough Properties reported on August 28 that it finalized the sale of the 232 A Street development site to P&G Gillette for the company's planned Grooming Headquarters and Technical Innovation Center. The 2.4-acre site has approval for an approximately 325,000-square-foot research and development campus, and Gillette has said it plans to invest nearly $1 billion in the new center. The closed land transaction is a concrete project milestone, but no specific vendor procurement is stated.
why: Nearly $1 billion headquarters and innovation-center plan

items.title: T Market opened its Massachusetts flagship at Natick Mall
items.description: T Market held the grand opening for its Massachusetts flagship at Natick Mall on August 27. The store combines grocery, Asian beauty, a food hall and bakery, and the company publicly lists a purchasing contact. The direct purchasing channel keeps this relevant immediately after opening without implying that any specific purchase is currently open.
why: Public purchasing contact is listed by the company

items.title: Maersk is opening a 617,000-square-foot fulfillment hub in Hopedale
items.description: Maersk says its new $100 million Hopedale fulfillment hub will begin operations in late August 2026, create approximately 1,000 jobs and support high-volume e-commerce fulfillment. The scale and near-term launch make this a strong operating-services signal, but no specific local vendor request is stated.

items.title: CPS Technologies leased an 80,000-square-foot Attleboro manufacturing facility
items.description: CPS Technologies signed a long-term lease for approximately 80,000 square feet at 523 Pleasant Street in Attleboro, about twice the size of its current Norton location. A subsequent lease filing says the company intends to relocate corporate offices, manufacturing and product development during 2027, with a construction period running through May 31, 2027. The lease provides for up to $3.2 million in landlord-funded qualifying improvements after CPS first spends at least $1.6 million. This is a concrete buildout and relocation signal, not evidence that any specific vendor package is currently open.
why: 80,000-square-foot long-term lease at a specific Attleboro address
Lease provides up to $3.2M for qualifying improvements after CPS first spends at least $1.6M

items.title: Bicara Therapeutics signed for a 35,090-square-foot new Boston headquarters
items.description: Bicara Therapeutics disclosed that it entered a sub-sublease with Wayfair for approximately 35,090 square feet at 10 St. James Avenue to serve as its new corporate headquarters. The term is scheduled to begin on the later of October 1, 2026 or execution of required consents. The committed relocation creates a defined pre-move window for workplace, IT and facility services, but the filing does not state that any vendor procurement is open.
why: SEC-filed lease creates a concrete relocation signal

items.title: Tori Japan is preparing four new Greater Boston restaurants
items.location: Boston, Malden, Taunton and Dorchester, MA
items.description: A Tori Japan representative confirmed plans for four new Massachusetts-area restaurants in Boston, Malden, Taunton and Dorchester. The first, an approximately 3,000-square-foot location at 961 Commonwealth Avenue near Boston University, is expected to open in late September, with Malden and Taunton locations targeted around the end of 2026. The multi-location rollout creates several pre-opening vendor windows, but no vendor solicitation is stated.
why: First approximately 3,000-square-foot restaurant targets late September
Additional Malden and Taunton openings are targeted by year-end

items.title: Big Y is preparing to open a new Saugus supermarket
items.description: Big Y lists Saugus among its grand-opening locations, with a September 10 opening date for the approximately 46,000-square-foot supermarket. The site is a strong pre-opening operations signal rather than a confirmed vendor request.
why: New recurring operating needs are plausible

items.title: Hawksmoor is opening a large Boston restaurant on September 8
items.description: Hawksmoor says its first Boston restaurant will open September 8 in Fort Point. Boston.com reports the new steakhouse will seat roughly 280 guests. The imminent full-service restaurant launch creates plausible recurring operating and facility-service needs, but no specific vendor solicitation is stated.

items.title: Forman Mills is opening its first Springfield store on September 17
items.description: Forman Mills says it will open its first Springfield location on September 17, 2026, marking the off-price retailer's 50th store. The company says the opening will create local jobs and introduce a large-format retail operation to the market. The pre-opening timing makes this a useful operating-services signal, but no specific local vendor solicitation is stated.
why: First Springfield location and 50th store systemwide
Large-format retail operation with recurring site-service needs

items.title: SMC is expanding its Devens medical-device manufacturing campus
items.description: Massachusetts awarded SMC $1.25 million to renovate its existing 330,000-square-foot Devens facility and construct a new 100,000-square-foot building. The project includes HVAC, power, injection-molding and building-system work and is expected to create new jobs.
items.sourceName: Massachusetts Executive Office of Economic Development

items.title: Autonodyne is building an autonomy demonstration and training center in Boston
items.description: Massachusetts awarded Autonodyne $1 million for construction and equipment for a 6,500-square-foot autonomy demonstration center with simulator stations, secure collaboration space, IT systems and training areas. The state says the company anticipates sourcing most project work from Massachusetts-based vendors.
why: Project includes IT, simulator and training infrastructure
Company anticipates sourcing most project work from Massachusetts vendors
items.sourceName: Massachusetts Executive Office of Economic Development

items.title: Helfrich Bros. plans a new 65,000-square-foot Lawrence manufacturing facility
items.description: Massachusetts awarded Helfrich Bros. $1 million to help acquire adjacent land and construct a new 65,000-square-foot manufacturing facility with cranes, welding equipment, an automated paint booth and a testing station. The project is expected to create jobs and support local suppliers.
why: State announcement notes support for local suppliers
items.sourceName: Massachusetts Executive Office of Economic Development

items.title: Degree Wellness is preparing its first two Massachusetts studios
items.description: Degree Wellness franchisees plan the brand's first two Massachusetts studios at 1158 Beacon Street, Unit 3 in Newton and 51A Church Street in Wellesley. The Newton studio is expected to debut within the next couple of months, with Wellesley to follow shortly after, and founding memberships are already being sold. The active launch preparation creates plausible facility and operating-service needs, but no vendor solicitation is stated.
why: Newton opening expected within the next couple of months
Founding-membership sales indicate active launch preparation

items.title: Zealand Pharma is preparing a new U.S. research hub in Cambridge
items.description: Zealand Pharma is preparing a Cambridge research hub expected to become operational in September 2026 and serve as its primary U.S. address. The lab-focused site is intended to support AI-driven drug discovery, automation and research expansion.

items.title: Advocates began renovation of a new 80,000-square-foot Marlborough headquarters
items.description: Construction has begun on an 80,000-square-foot interior renovation that will turn 251 Locke Drive into Advocates' new headquarters and training center, with completion targeted for fall 2026. The general contractor, architect and MEP engineer are already identified, so the strongest remaining prospecting angles are workplace technology, AV, furniture, move-in, security, cleaning and ongoing facility services rather than core construction awards.
why: Fall 2026 completion creates a defined move-in window

items.title: Session House is renovating a Dorchester pub space for a fall opening
items.description: Session House is preparing to take over the former Scobie's Cafe & Bar at 782 Adams Street as an Irish-inspired music, dining and social venue. Light renovations are currently underway, with an early-to-mid-fall 2026 opening expected. The restaurant-and-live-music format creates several plausible vendor categories, but no vendor solicitation is stated.
why: Restaurant plus live-music operation creates several recurring service categories

items.title: Kima Café is preparing to open in Somerville in mid-September
items.description: Boston.com reports that Kima Café, a new concept from the team behind Glasser Coffee Co., is targeting a mid-September opening at 75 Bow Street in Somerville. The café will serve specialty coffee, Asian-influenced drinks and a food menu. The defined opening window creates plausible pre-opening and recurring operating-service needs, but no vendor solicitation is stated.
why: New physical café with food service

items.title: Babilou Family US is opening an early-education center in Allston in September
items.description: Babilou Family US says its new infant-through-pre-K center at the Enterprise Research Campus in Allston will open in September 2026. A new childcare facility can create recurring facility, janitorial, security and operating-supply needs, but no purchasing request is stated.
why: Recurring facility and operating needs are plausible

items.title: Boston Dynamics is developing a 330,000-square-foot Waltham robotics center
items.description: Massachusetts says a Business Builds award will support renovation and buildout of approximately 330,000 square feet in Waltham for robotics manufacturing, training, R&D and related operations. The project supports significant planned job creation.
items.sourceName: Massachusetts Executive Office of Economic Development

items.title: Lowe's Donuts is preparing a second bakery in Newburyport for late September
items.description: Lowe's Donuts announced a second location in Newburyport that is slated to open in late September 2026. The new shop will add seating and a coffee and specialty-drink program, and the business is already hiring for the location. The active pre-opening period creates plausible supply and operating-service needs, but no vendor procurement is stated and the exact street address has not yet been published.
why: Second location adds seating and a new beverage program
Hiring is already underway for the Newburyport shop

items.title: Ratio Therapeutics signed a 17,000-square-foot office expansion in Boston's Seaport
items.description: Ratio Therapeutics signed a 17,000-square-foot office lease expansion at Boston's Innovation & Design Building, keeping the radiopharmaceutical developer in the Seaport while increasing its footprint. The executed expansion creates plausible workplace, IT and facility-service needs, but no vendor solicitation is stated.
why: Life-sciences company increasing its Boston footprint
Concrete lease signal rather than speculative site search

items.title: Colette Bakery is preparing a fourth Boston-area location in Arlington
items.description: Colette Bakery is preparing a new 20-seat café at 681 Massachusetts Avenue in Arlington and hopes to hold its grand opening before the end of September. The owners told What Now Boston that the team has already begun hiring. The active fit-out and hiring period creates plausible local vendor needs, but no procurement request is stated.
why: Targeting a grand opening before the end of September

items.title: Achilito's Taqueria is preparing a fourth location near Fenway and Back Bay
items.description: Achilito's Taqueria confirmed plans for a new approximately 2,300-square-foot location at 1114 Boylston Street, targeting a late-October 2026 opening. The expansion creates a defined pre-opening window for restaurant operating services and supplies, but no vendor solicitation has been announced.
why: Fourth location for an expanding local chain

items.title: Image Analysis Group opened a new U.S. office in Cambridge
items.description: Image Analysis Group announced the opening of a new Cambridge office to expand its U.S. clinical-trial imaging operations and business development presence. The company says it plans local hiring across clinical imaging operations, data science, regulatory support and business development over the next 12 to 24 months. The office is already open, so this is primarily an ongoing workplace and growth-services signal rather than a pre-opening buildout opportunity.
why: Local hiring planned over the next 12 to 24 months
Expansion places operational and business-development teams in Massachusetts
items.sourceName: Image Analysis Group via EIN Presswire

items.title: SOVE signed a 10-year lease for a new Boston Theatre District cafe
items.description: SOVE signed a 10-year lease for approximately 1,100 square feet at 62 Boylston Street in Boston's Theatre District. The lease commenced August 13, construction is expected to begin soon, and the Japanese- and Korean-inspired cafe is targeting an early-2027 opening. This is an early fit-out and pre-opening signal; no specific vendor solicitation has been announced.
why: Construction is expected to begin soon
Early-stage cafe buildout leaves a longer pre-opening prospecting window
items.sourceName: Boston Real Estate Times / The Hamilton Company
